research_rationale:
EO 9245 (7 FR 7328, September 16, 1942; held official Federal Register text) transferred the functions, powers and duties of the United States High Commissioner to the Philippine Islands, with the personnel, records, property and funds of the office, to the Secretary of the Interior. Paragraph 1 of EO 9616 (10 FR 11837, signed September 14, 1945; held Federal Register text) states "Executive Order No. 9245 of Sep­
tember 16, 1942, is hereby repealed" and transfers the same functions, personnel, records, property and funds back from the Secretary of the Interior to the High Commissioner. EO 9616 has no deferred-effect wording, so the transfer to the Secretary ended on 1945-09-14 and the order was not in force on 2026-10-14.
savings_reason: The functions, powers, duties, personnel, records, property and funds that EO 9245 moved to the Secretary of the Interior are transferred back to the High Commissioner by paragraph 1 of EO 9616; no U.S. Code or eCFR citation of EO 9245 was found by the bounded searches.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held texts citing EO 9245 by number: only EO 9616 (Federal Register text and two APP transcription files) names it. The order has no sunset or condition. The transfer was made under the First War Powers Act, 1941, but no held source shows that authority or the office ended before 1945-09-14. No earlier end, amendment or partial revocation is held.
scope_check: EO 9245 has a single operative sentence, which paragraph 1 of EO 9616 repeals as a whole by number and date; the repeal is not partial. EO 9616 then re-establishes the transfer in the opposite direction under its own paragraphs 1 to 14, which are new commands of EO 9616.
independent_command_check: The order has one command (the transfer of functions, personnel, records, property and funds). It created no body and no separate duty, and the reverse transfer in EO 9616 leaves nothing of EO 9245 in force.
savings_check: The transfer of functions, personnel, records, property and funds is a completed transfer whose consequences were reversed by paragraph 1 of EO 9616, which returns them to the High Commissioner; the held text of EO 9616 has no separate saving clause. Whatever accrued to the Secretary of the Interior under the 1942 transfer is the subject of the reverse transfer, not of a surviving command under EO 9245.

research_rationale: EO 10472 (18 FR 4247, July 20, 1953; held official Federal Register text) established the National Agricultural Advisory Commission to advise the Secretary of Agriculture, with its membership and terms (section 1), its advisory duty and meetings (section 2) and a no-funds-pending-appropriation rule (section 3). EO 10937 of May 3, 1961 restated section 1 (an amendment, not an end; its Federal Register copy is held only as a custody record, so it is disclosed here but not cited as a source). EO 11256 of November 4, 1965 (30 FR 14137) revoked EO 10472 and EO 10937 in its section 7 and established a new Committee and Commission in the same order. Every clause therefore ended on 1965-11-04 and the order was not in force on 2026-10-14. The inventory is corrected because the machine span missed section 1 and the first part of section 2 (columns misordered in the held scan).
savings_reason: EO 11256 has no saving provision; the bounded U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog searches found only the amendment by EO 10937 and the revocation by EO 11256 and no citation of EO 10472 as a current authority.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held texts citing EO 10472 by number: EO 10937 (amends section 1) and EO 11256 (revokes) are the only later instruments, plus their transcription copies. The order states no sunset: members serve fixed terms and successors are appointed for three years, and section 3 only withholds Federal funds until an appropriation exists. No held source shows the Commission dissolved or the order ended before 1965-11-04.
scope_check: EO 11256 section 7 revokes EO 10472 as a whole by number and date (together with EO 10937); it is not a partial revocation. EO 10937 amended only section 1, restating it in full; no held source shows sections 2 or 3 amended, and the section 1 restatement is disclosed but not cited as a later event because its Federal Register copy is held only as a custody record.
independent_command_check: The only free-standing command besides the establishment is section 3, which restricts expenditure of Federal funds on the Commission until a specific appropriation exists; it presupposes the Commission and falls with the order. EO 11256 creates a new Committee and Commission under its own sections and does not continue any command of EO 10472.
savings_check: EO 11256 has no savings clause in the text read (sections 1 to 7). Members appointed under EO 10472 or EO 10937 are not said to continue; EO 11256 section 6 separately terminates its own Committee and Commission ninety days after the final report. The U.S. Code and eCFR bounded searches found no citation of EO 10472.

research_rationale: EO 10679 (21 FR 7199, September 20, 1956; held official Federal Register text) prescribed regulations for agreements between the Secretary of Defense and the States on withholding State retirement contributions from the pay of civilian Army and Air National Guard employees under the act of June 15, 1956. Section 8 of EO 10996 of February 16, 1962 states "This order supersedes Executive Order No. 10679 of" September 20, 1956, and restates each of its commands in sections 1 to 6 of EO 10996 with the 1961 amendments. Every clause therefore ended on 1962-02-16 and the order was not in force on 2026-10-14. The machine inventory is corrected: paragraph 1 was one 12,448-character clause that swallowed a page break and unrelated contents pages, so it is split into its two real fragments. The U.S. Code note at 5 U.S.C. 5518 prints EO 10996 including its section 8, which agrees.
savings_reason: Section 7 of EO 10996 continues agreements and other actions taken under affected functions, so State agreements already entered under EO 10679 survive as independent instruments until amended, modified or terminated by appropriate authority; the order's own commands do not survive.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held texts citing EO 10679 by number: only EO 10996 (Federal Register text and APP transcription) is a later instrument; the other hits are the order's own text. The order has no sunset or condition, and its 120-day time limit applies to each State request, not to the order. No amendment, partial revocation or earlier supersession is held, so nothing precedes 1962-02-16.
scope_check: Section 8 of EO 10996 supersedes EO 10679 as a whole by number and date. Each of the eight corrected clauses has a counterpart in EO 10996 sections 1 to 6, which is why the whole order, not part of it, is superseded; the authority to prescribe rules in paragraph 6 is re-delegated in section 6 of EO 10996.
independent_command_check: Individual agreements already made between the Secretary of Defense and a State under EO 10679 are separate instruments; section 7 of EO 10996 keeps them in force until amended, modified or terminated. They are not commands of EO 10679 and do not keep any clause of this order operative, so they are treated as savings, not as an independent command.
savings_check: Section 7 of EO 10996 continues determinations, regulations, agreements and other actions taken with respect to a function affected by EO 10996 and not revoked, superseded or made inapplicable before its date, except to the extent inconsistent with it. Agreements made under EO 10679 therefore continue as agreements, but EO 10679 itself is superseded; the continuing instruments are independent of this order.

research_rationale: EO 10816 (24 FR 3777, signed May 7, 1959; held official Federal Register text) amended Executive Order No. 10501 of November 5, 1953 (safeguarding official information) in three paragraphs: a new subparagraph of section 4, a new Historical Research subparagraph of section 15, and a restated first sentence of section 8(d). EO 11652 section 14 supersedes EO 10501 as amended by EO 10816 and the other listed amending orders as of its effective date, and section 15 makes it effective June 1, 1972, so each clause ended on 1972-06-01 and the order was not in force on 2026-10-14. The inventory is corrected (paragraph 1 had been omitted). EO 11652 itself describes EO 10816 as of May 8, 1959, the filing date, while the register signing date is May 7, 1959; the same instrument is meant. EO 10964 later rewrote section 4 of EO 10501 (a later event on clause 1, not an end).
savings_reason: EO 11652 supersedes EO 10501 as amended and its transitional provisions concern previously classified information, not the commands EO 10816 added; the bounded U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog searches found no continuing authority citing EO 10816.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held texts citing EO 10816 by number: EO 11652 (Federal Register text and APP transcription) is the only text that disposes of it; EO 10964 (September 20, 1961) rewrote section 4 of EO 10501, EO 10901, 10985, 11097 and 11382 amended only section 2 lists of EO 10501 (read in the held texts), and EO 11171 states it does not modify or supersede EO 10501. scope_check: The supersession names EO 10501 as amended by EO 10816 and is whole-order for the parent, so every amendment text inside it ended with it. independent_command_check: EO 10816 contains only amendment instructions to EO 10501 and no free-standing command, body or deadline; nothing in it survives the supersession of the parent order.
savings_check: EO 11652 contains transitional rules for information classified under EO 10501 (the held effective-date provisions deal with review of previously classified material); they do not preserve the access, transmission or section 4 rules added by EO 10816. The classification markings are independent effects of past actions, not commands of EO 10816.

research_rationale: EO 10938 (26 FR 3951, May 4, 1961; held official Federal Register text) established the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board (sec. 1), set its review and reporting duties (sec. 2), provided for its members and payment (sec. 3) and revoked EO 10656 (sec. 4, inside the inventory span of the third clause). Section 6 of EO 11460 (March 20, 1969; 34 FR 5535) states "Executive Order No. 10938 of May 4,1961, is hereby revoked." and the same order re-establishes a Board under its own terms. The first and last end of every clause is therefore 1969-03-20 and the order was not in force on 2026-10-14. The held U.S. Code editorial note at 50 U.S.C. 3023 says EO 10938 was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 11460, Mar. 20, 1969, which agrees.
savings_reason: EO 11460 has no saving provision; the bounded U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog searches show only the revocation (the U.S. Code note at 50 U.S.C. 3023 repeats it) and no citation of EO 10938 as a current authority.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held texts citing EO 10938 by number: EO 11460 (APP transcription and Federal Register text) is the only later instrument; the other hits are the order's own text and a duplicate file. The order has no sunset or condition. Own-term leads (reports every six months, payment from the Special Projects appropriation for 1961 and later years) are continuing duties, not ends. No earlier abolition, termination or amendment of the Board is held, so nothing precedes 1969-03-20.
scope_check: The revocation names the whole order by number and date; it is not a revocation of a part and has no qualifier. EO 10938 section 4 revoked EO 10656, which is a completed one-time revocation executed on signing in 1961 and is not revived by the later revocation of EO 10938; that act sits inside the third clause span, whose continuing commands (compensation and payment) end on 1969-03-20.
independent_command_check: EO 11460 re-establishes the Board with similar duties, but under its own sections 1 to 5; those are new commands of EO 11460, not continuation of EO 10938. The Board, its advisory duty, the access-to-information duty and the payment rule of EO 10938 all fall with the revocation, and nothing in EO 11460 keeps any of them in force under EO 10938.
savings_check: EO 11460 contains no savings clause (sections 1 to 6 read). Members appointed under EO 10938 are not said to continue. The only surviving legal effect of EO 10938 is the earlier revocation of EO 10656 (section 4), which is a completed act and independent of the order's force.

research_rationale: EO 11962 (42 FR 4323, January 19, 1977; held official Federal Register text) established the President's Advisory Board on International Investment and its supporting duties, with its own sunset of December 31, 1978 unless sooner extended. EO 12007 of August 22, 1977 terminated the Board (section 5(a)) and revoked EO 11962 (section 5(b), "(b ) Executive Order No. 11962 of January 19, 1977, is revoked."), which is earlier than the own-terms sunset. Every clause therefore ended on 1977-08-22 and the order was not in force on 2026-10-14. The inventory is corrected to add section 1(a), omitted by the machine segmentation. The held U.S. Code note at 22 U.S.C. 3107 says EO 11962 was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12007, Aug. 22, 1977, 42 F.R. 42839, which agrees.
savings_reason: EO 12007 has no saving provision. The bounded U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog searches found only the revocation (the 22 U.S.C. 3107 note repeats it) and no later citation of EO 11962 as a current authority.
earlier_end_check: Searched the held texts citing EO 11962 by number: only EO 12007 (Federal Register text and APP transcription) is a later instrument. The own-terms end (section 6, December 31, 1978) is later than the revocation, so the earliest end is 1977-08-22. No amendment, extension or earlier termination of the Board appears in the held sources. Section 6 of EO 12007 supersedes subsections of EO 11948 that extended other committees to December 31, 1978; it does not concern EO 11962 and does not extend it.
scope_check: EO 12007 revokes EO 11962 as a whole by number and date and separately terminates the Board; no part is excepted. The machine inventory missed section 1(a); the corrected inventory has nine clauses covering every operative sentence between the preamble and the signature, and each is ended by the same instrument.
independent_command_check: The supporting commands (the Executive Director's staff and administrative services, the Executive Secretary appointment, the Federal Advisory Committee Act functions performed by the Executive Director, member compensation) all exist only for the Board and are within the revoked order; none is a free-standing command that survives the Board's termination.
